title: Premium Payment, Underpayment and Refund Payee — NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
### Premium payment terms for NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)

NFIP premium is payable in full for the term: the full premium accompanies the application or renewal and no installment plan exists.

*Clause no longer in force:* "A payment is accepted only by one of the accepted payment methods and is applied to the policy and term named on the payment; it is never moved to another policy of the same customer." This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis.

**Escrow.** When a lender pays from escrow the payment method is escrow disbursement and the policy's premium payor is the lender's escrow account.

**Underpayment.** When the amount received at application is less than the total term premium, Tidemark sends an underpayment notice and the policyholder has the tier's underpayment cure period, in calendar days from the notice, to pay the difference; if the difference is not received, the limits are reduced to the amounts the premium received will buy and the difference is not pursued.

**Overpayment.** When the amount received exceeds the total due, the excess is refunded to the payor in the same way as a cancellation refund.

**Dishonored payment.** A dishonored payment is reversed and, when it was the application premium, the policy is nullified under the reason Premium Payment Dishonored.

*Clause no longer in force:* "Every refund is paid to the payor of record: payee lender escrow when the premium payor is the lender's escrow account, and payee insured otherwise." This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis.

| Situation at application | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Amount received equals the total term premium | Premium paid in full |
| Amount received is less than the total term premium | Underpayment notice; the difference is payable within the cure period; if unpaid, limits are reduced to what the premium received buys and the difference is not pursued |
| Amount received exceeds the total due | Excess refunded to the payor in the same way as a cancellation refund |
| Application premium dishonored | Payment reversed; policy nullified under Premium Payment Dishonored |

*Hypothetical case.* A policy whose total term premium is 1,200.00 dollars receives 1,000.00 dollars at application. Tidemark's underpayment notice opens the cure period; if the 200.00-dollar difference does not arrive within it, the limits are reduced to what 1,000.00 dollars of premium buys, and the 200.00 dollars is not pursued.

superseded_clauses: A payment is accepted only by one of the accepted_payment_methods and is applied to the policy and term named on the payment; it is never moved to another policy of the same customer.
Every refund is paid to the payor of record: payee LENDER_ESCROW when premium_payor is LENDER_ESCROW, and payee INSURED otherwise.
